Can someone with more knowledge than me explain how this is possible?

Here's the writeup: http://www.flintbox.com/public/project/6027/

It's not completely clear, but I think the droplets are slightly different distances from the center, so they only appear to mix. Could be wrong though.

One of the plates of the container is stationary while the other one can freely rotate. Inside the container they place viscous fluids (like syrup). When the top plate is rotated at a constant speed, a shear stress gradient forms in the fluid due to friction between the molecules. When rotated the opposite direction, an inverse shear gradient forms and effectively returns all the molecules to their original location.

It is a really good example of mechanical stress that is really hard to see in solids. Essentially the rotating plate applies mechanical load to the fluid, and due to viscous friction, stress develops between the molecules, just as it does in the little polarized beam. When the load is removed, the stress is removed as well, and both the beam and the fluid return to their original unloaded shapes.
